summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with psoriatic arthritis on immunosuppressive therapy was readmitted for worsening left leg pain and erythema one day after discharge. Imaging revealed a complex fluid collection in the left calf concerning for abscess, leading to treatment with IV antibiotics including vancomycin and Zosyn. An ultrasound-guided aspiration yielded purulent fluid with no organisms seen on gram stain and no growth on culture. Due to lack of improvement, the patient underwent incision and drainage of the abscess, followed by a muscle biopsy that showed only inflammatory changes without evidence of fungal or mycobacterial infection. He developed transient acute kidney injury and hypernatremia, both managed supportively. He experienced episodes of confusion and a fall, with brain imaging showing no acute abnormalities, likely due to medication effects. The infection resolved with treatment, and he was discharged home with a PICC line for continued IV antibiotics, wound care, and follow-up arranged with rheumatology and home health.
